description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and various accuracy metrics, including Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis, labeled Initial Confidence, has a linear scale, ranging from 0.81 to 0.99 with a tick label interval of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled Accuracy, also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0 with a tick label interval of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy, represented by a solid blue line with error bars, starts at approximately 0.95 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations, and ends at around 0.96 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99; Δ Accuracy, depicted by a dashed orange line with error bars, begins at about 0.4 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, generally decreases with some fluctuations, and ends at roughly 0.07 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99; Initial Accuracy, shown as a dash-dot green line with error bars, starts at approximately 0.55 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, exhibits an overall increasing trend with some fluctuations, and ends at around 0.93 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99.
